text:
sara: FYI team, noticed a repeat dashboards SLO breach this morning tied to query fanout + RBAC checks. 3rd time this week, higher p95 on small widgets. Logs attached below.

alex: ugh, saw the alert too. can you paste the sample trace? is this the slow-path authz check that hits authz-service for each subquery?

sara: yep. sample trace:
```
TRACE 2026-01-10T09:12:12Z dashboard-query id=abc123 stage=fanout -> authz-check route=/panels/metrics shard=17 took=320ms
TRACE 2026-01-10T09:12:12Z dashboard-query id=abc123 stage=fetch shard=17 took=18ms
TRACE 2026-01-10T09:12:12Z dashboard-query id=abc123 stage=fanout -> authz-check route=/panels/alerts shard=4 took=410ms
```
Essentially each child query does an authz RPC to permissions-svc. Under load that service peeks to upstream store and adds 200-400ms.

ben: that matches the profiles from the load test. authz-service latency + per-fanout roundtrip kills tail. two obvious levers: (1) push authz earlier (prefilter/predicate) or (2) cache authz results per-request/key. both have tradeoffs.

maya: +1. Prefiltering would let us prune some subqueries before we do work, but correctness for dynamic permissions (role changes, revokes) is a concern. caching reduces RPCs but increases complexity around invalidation.

alex: thinking out loud: what if we introduce a short-lived TTL cache scoped to the dashboard request + user-epoch token? i.e., on request start we fetch a user-epoch (cheap monotonic token) and use that as cache key for permission checks for the lifetime of the request. no long-lived state, invalidation becomes a no-op (new epoch -> new cache).

ben: that could work. two followups: (a) how do we get epoch cheaply without a remote call for every request? (b) need to bound memory per-host to avoid explosion with many concurrent requests. suggestion: epoch is part of auth cookie/token issued by authn layer, refreshed on changes. if not present, fallback to a single authn call (rare).

jamie: also consider an ACL delta stream per org for Dedicated/Private customers. push deltas to edge nodes so policy checks can be local. more infra but near-zero per-fanout RTT. downside: harder to operate and more memory.

maya: for Hosted tiers we probably can't push deltas for every tenant. hybrid approach: request-scoped cache (alex) + optional background delta sync for high-traffic customers.

sara: we should also audit where we do authz: some panels still check on each shard; could we centralize a precompute step that maps queries -> required-permissions, evaluate once, then filter fanout list? saves duplicate checks.

alex: +1. sketch: pipeline step A: compute required-permissions by analyzing the query graph. B: fetch perms once per effective-user-epoch. C: filter fanout nodes. D: execute pruned fanout.

ben: sound plan. perf numbers? In the load test we saw 35% p95 reduction when we eliminated repeated authz calls on identical checks. combined with TTL cache we estimated 60% p95 improvement.

sara: action items: (1) prototype request-scoped permission cache in console-query (alex + ben), (2) add query-to-perm analyzer to pipeline (sara + jamie), (3) run focused load test reproducing RBAC fanout pattern (ben) — aim for canary in staging in 2 weeks.

alex: I'll start a branch for the cache shim, minimal config flag: `authz.request_cache_ttl_ms` default 30000 (30s). will also add telemetry for cache hits/misses per request.

maya: add a safety: if cache hits < 10% under a rollout, rollback. keep correctness test harness to simulate revokes.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: staging cluster deploy scheduled for 2026-01-12 14:00 UTC (rolling). CI pipeline will run integration suite.

ben: cool, I'll add load test scenario and a synthetic dashboard with many small panels to simulate the fanout.

sara: thanks. let's reconvene after the prototype + load test. please post PRs/benchmarks in this thread. :thumbsup:
